changes.before: the fear of the prince of the eunuchs
changes.after: the fear of the eunuchs' prince

witness.bytes: The prince of the eunuchs said to Daniel, “I fear my lord the king, who has appointed your food and your drink. For why should he see your faces worse looking than the youths who are of your own age? Then you would endanger my head with the king.”

וַיֹּ֜אמֶר שַׂ֤ר הַסָּרִיסִים֙ לְדָ֣נִיֵּ֔אל יָרֵ֤א אֲנִי֙ אֶת אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מִנָּ֔ה אֶת מַאֲכַלְכֶ֖ם וְאֶת מִשְׁתֵּיכֶ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֡ר לָמָּה֩ יִרְאֶ֨ה אֶת פְּנֵיכֶ֜ם זֹֽעֲפִ֗ים מִן הַיְלָדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר כְּגִֽילְכֶ֔ם וְחִיַּבְתֶּ֥ם אֶת רֹאשִׁ֖י לַמֶּֽלֶךְ

changes.speaker_finding: In 1:10 the speaker of the fear is the chief officer of the eunuchs: WEB 1:10 opens with that officer as the subject of 'said to Daniel' and his speech begins 'I fear my lord the king'; OSHB/WLC Dan.1.10 opens with the verb of saying, then the two-word title (chief + the-eunuchs), then 'to Daniel', then the first-person 'I fear'. The steward is not named in the verse (he first appears at 1:11).
